extracted.intended_audience: women researchers seeking PRIMA career grants in Switzerland / applicants to the SNSF PRIMA scheme
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal eligibility/evaluation rules for applying to the SNSF PRIMA career grant (targeted at women researchers aiming for a professorship) including participation requirements, submission procedures, evaluation phases, and project/lifetime management rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target applicant profile / purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: PRIMA grants were aimed at talented women researchers demonstrating a high potential for obtaining a professorship. PRIMA grantees undertook an independent research project with their own team, at least at the group leader level, within a Swiss research institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should propose an independent project and demonstrate leadership at group-leader level; the grant is explicitly targeted to support career progression toward professorship. (Note: the last call was 1 November 2021 and the PRIMA budget has been reallocated to other SNSF career schemes.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctorate / equivalent qualification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers: have a doctorate (PhD) or at least three years of research activity after obtaining their higher education degree (equivalent qualification to a doctorate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant does not hold a PhD, they must demonstrate at least three years of research activity after the relevant higher-education degree that is considered equivalent to a doctorate (check PRIMA Regulations for formal interpretation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum post-doctoral research experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers: have acquired at least two years of research experience after their doctorate or equivalent qualification to a doctorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This two-year minimum must be satisfied by the submission deadline; see PRIMA Regulations for how research experience is counted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timing window (academic age)
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers: submit their application between two and ten years after their PhD defense or after the date of the equivalent qualification to a doctorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'academic age' (time since doctorate) is used to determine eligibility windows (2–10 years for typical researchers). For clinical scientists special rules apply. Time periods are calculated based on the relevant submission deadline for PRIMA applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical scientist eligibility and time window
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical scientists: have a medical exam (state examination or equivalent); have acquired at least three years of clinical work and at least 2 years of research activities after their medical exam; submit their application up to 14 years after their medical exam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical-track applicants use the medical exam date as the reference point; ensure clinical and research activity minimums are documented. The 14-year upper window applies to submission timing for clinical applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-period calculation rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The time periods are calculated on the basis of the relevant submission deadline for PRIMA applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When computing academic age, net academic age, and eligibility windows, use the official submission deadline as the reference date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net academic age consideration in evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the difference between the academic age and the net academic age? The academic age indicates how much time has passed since the doctorate. On the other hand, the net academic age indicates how much time you have been able to spend doing research since your doctorate; it is taken into account in the evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Net academic age is used by evaluators to account for career interruptions or reduced research time; applicants must declare and document reductions in research time in the net academic age form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobility statement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In the mobility statement, you should give reasons for your choice of research institution and set out your completed and planned mobility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the mobility statement to justify the institutional choice and to detail past and planned moves; this informs assessment of the project's fit and career strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net academic age form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In the form used to calculate the net academic age, you should indicate how much time you have been able to spend doing research since your doctorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the net academic age calculation form accurately, documenting parental leave, clinical duties, part-time work, or other factors that reduced research time, as this affects evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission platform and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The applications must be submitted via the mySNF platform. The mySNF platform will be opened for submission three months before the respective application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must use mySNF to submit; consult the 'Guidelines for submitting a PRIMA proposal' PDF and the platform guidance. Plan to prepare and upload all required documents before the platform opens/close dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation procedure (two phases)
rubrics_metrics.description: PRIMA applications are evaluated in two phases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page references an 'Evaluation procedure – this is how we select' document; applicants should consult that document for phase-by-phase criteria, review stages, and scoring rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult PRIMA Regulations for formal eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Please consult the PRIMA Regulations to determine your formal eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal eligibility rules, clauses, and definitions (including Clause 1.11 referenced for extensions) are in the PRIMA Regulations PDF; applicants must check the Regulations for binding rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of eligibility period for special circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The time window for submission of a PRIMA proposal can be extended if the applicant has suffered a delay due to one of the reasons stated in Clause 1.11 of the General implementation regulations for the Funding Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To request an extension, verify that your circumstance matches Clause 1.11 and follow the procedures described in the General implementation regulations; documentation will be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on number of re-applications
rubrics_metrics.description: How many times can I apply? Applicants whose request for a PRIMA grant was rejected may submit one further application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one additional (i.e., second) application is permitted after a rejection; plan resubmissions carefully and address prior reviewers' criticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: No exceptions for two-year post-doctoral minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: Are any exceptions possible for PRIMA regarding the minimum of two years' research work required after the doctorate? No exceptions can be granted. This requirement needs to be met by the submission deadline, with the date of the exam or thesis defence being the relevant date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect waivers for the two-year minimum; ensure documentation proves the two-year post-doctoral research period by the submission deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on parallel submission with SNSF project under evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot submit a PRIMA proposal if you have an SNSF project under evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you currently have an SNSF proposal under review, wait until that review concludes before submitting a PRIMA application. Consult SNSF rules about overlapping submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction if you have an approved/ongoing SNSF project
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have an approved or ongoing SNSF project, you cannot submit a PRIMA proposal for the same funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check project dates and avoid requesting overlapping funding periods; consider timing or coordination with existing SNSF projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for transferring an entire grant to a new Swiss research institution
rubrics_metrics.description: You can transfer your grant to another institution, including the funds covering your salary, but you must contact the SNSF explaining the reasons for the move as well as its added value for your project or your career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A written request by the grantee should include: confirmation letters from the new research institution (as with the initial institution) and written acknowledgement from an authorized body of the former institution. The SNSF evaluates the request considering the project’s feasibility and the relevance to pursue your career in the new institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant termination if taking a job outside academic research
rubrics_metrics.description: What happens to my grant if I take on a new job outside of academic research? You must inform the SNSF accordingly. The SNSF terminates the grant. The remaining amount of the grant must be refunded to the SNSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify SNSF immediately if leaving academia; expect termination and financial reconciliation including refund of unspent funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting documents and forms required
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents & downloads: PRIMA Regulations; Written confirmation of the research institution; Guidelines for submitting a PRIMA proposal (English version).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must prepare and upload the prescribed forms (institutional confirmation, mobility/net-age forms, CV in required format) and follow the Guidelines and Regulations PDFs for exact document content and formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary measures available to projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary measures such as Mobility grants in projects, Flexibility Grant, Media training, Gender equality grant are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may request or use supplementary measures within projects; consult the documents on 'Supplementary measures' for eligibility, application, and integration into the project budget and plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career progression timing after PRIMA (Eccellenza Professorial Fellowship eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: PRIMA grantees can apply for an SNSF Eccellenza Professorial Fellowship 18 months after starting their PRIMA grant at the earliest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan career timeline accordingly if aiming to progress from PRIMA to Eccellenza; note the 18-month minimum start-to-application interval.
